answer: Agents can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a scarce deposit before it can bid, vote, or earn reputation, then assigning tasks through random committees whose members cross-check signed work. A cluster of fake agents must fund every identity and risks correlated slashing when their outputs or collusion patterns match, so creating thousands is expensive and financially fragile. The wharf, saffron, and quartz markets therefore reward long-lived honest identities.
